answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each agent identity to prove control of a hardware-backed attestation key and run code matching an approved MRENCLAVE; a copied VM cannot forge that proof. MRENCLAVE identifies enclave code, not a unique machine, so deployments must also bind identities to platform credentials and enforce registration limits. This makes scaling costly in genuine silicon, not mere VM duplication—a vine of agents still needs a trusted bridge to hardware, even under a zephyr of cloned images.
